title: I made a free Windows + Android app where 12 AI agents debate a stock and give a Buy/Hold/Sell rating (TradingAgents framework)
author: jisrawia
selftext:
I've been playing with TradingAgents, an open-source framework from Tauric Research that runs a stock through a team of LLM agents set up like a trading desk:

Download (Windows installer + Android APK): [https://github.com/ajisrawi/TradingAgents-Apps](https://github.com/ajisrawi/TradingAgents-Apps)

\- 4 analysts: market (price and technical indicators), sentiment (StockTwits and Reddit posts), news, and fundamentals (financials and SEC filings)

\- a bull researcher and a bear researcher who argue over the analysts' reports

\- a research manager who settles the debate

\- a trader who drafts a plan

\- 3 risk managers (aggressive, neutral, conservative) who push back on it

\- a portfolio manager who makes the final call: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight or Sell

It only ran as a Python command-line tool, so I built two standalone apps around it:

\- Windows: download the installer and run it. No Python, no terminal.

\- Android: the whole framework runs on the phone itself. No PC or server needed.

The video shows a full run of the desktop app

What you can do:

\- Analyze any ticker on Yahoo Finance: US stocks, ETFs, international (e.g. 0700.HK) and crypto (BTC-USD)

\- Pick which analysts to use and how deep the debate goes (1, 3 or 5 rounds)

\- Pick a date in the past to see what the agents would have said with the data available then

\- Watch each agent work live and read every report, including the full bull vs. bear debate

\- Keep a history of past runs. The framework also remembers its earlier calls on a ticker and checks them against what the price actually did, then feeds those lessons into the next run

\- Use your own model: OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, or a local model through Ollama / LM Studio. Your API key stays on your device

What it does NOT do:

\- It doesn't connect to a broker or place trades. It's a research tool that produces a rating and a written thesis.

\- It isn't backtested alpha. LLM agents arguing about a stock is interesting and sometimes surprisingly sharp, but treat the output as a second opinion, not a signal. Not financial advice.

\- One run makes dozens of LLM calls and takes a few minutes, billed to your own key. A cheap model is fine for trying it out.

The Android app has been tested on the emulator so far, so reports from real phones are welcome. I'm not affiliated with Tauric Research; the agent design is theirs, I built the apps

Curious what you'd want the agents to look at that they don't yet, and which models give the most sensible debates.
